title: Study and Focus Listening Guide
content: For studying, coding, reading, and deep work, prefer steady low-to-medium energy tracks, softer textures, and moods like focused, chill, or peaceful. Lofi, ambient, and classical tracks reduce distraction because they usually have smooth dynamics and fewer sharp changes.

title: Workout and Running Listening Guide
content: For gym sessions, running, and high-intensity movement, favor high energy, strong tempo, and high danceability. Drum and bass, house, pop, rock, afrobeat, and latin songs usually support momentum better than very acoustic or low-tempo tracks.

title: Wind-Down and Sleep Listening Guide
content: For winding down, journaling, late-night reading, or sleep preparation, recommend low energy, high acousticness, and calmer moods. Ambient, classical, folk, jazz, and soft lofi are safer choices than aggressive or very bright high-tempo songs.

title: Party and Social Energy Guide
content: For parties, group hangouts, and social playlists, prioritize upbeat valence, danceability, and accessible grooves. House, latin, k-pop, afrobeat, pop, reggae, and gospel can work well depending on the requested mood.

title: Commute and Errand Listening Guide
content: For commuting, errands, or walking around, recommend medium-to-high energy songs that feel active but not overwhelming. Synthwave, indie pop, hip hop, reggae, and pop can fit because they balance rhythm, mood, and replayability.

title: Heartbreak and Reflective Mood Guide
content: For sad, reflective, rainy, or breakup requests, recommend songs that match the mood without claiming to fix someone's emotions. Folk, blues, r&b, cinematic, and slower acoustic tracks can validate the requested tone while staying gentle.

title: Recommendation Diversity Rule
content: When confidence is reasonable, avoid returning only near-duplicates. Keep the best match first, then include at least one adjacent genre or mood when the catalog has a strong enough alternative. Explain the trade-off so the user understands why a slightly different song appears.

title: Responsible Music Recommendation Boundary
content: The recommender should not claim to diagnose emotions, guarantee productivity, or infer sensitive traits from music taste. It should present recommendations as suggestions based on stated preferences and catalog metadata, and it should flag vague or risky inputs for human review.
